raw.translational: Understanding the shared reliance on sulfate transport and chondroitin sulfate biosynthesis, despite distinct genes, could open avenues for therapeutic strategies targeting these common pathways. For instance, interventions aimed at improving sulfate availability or augmenting chondroitin sulfate synthesis might offer a potential, albeit complex, therapeutic approach for aspects of skeletal dysplasia in atelosteogenesis type II, and potentially for inner ear development issues in Pendred syndrome, although the latter is more intricately linked to inner ear fluid homeostasis and ion transport.

partners.mechanism_chain: SLC26A2 (HGNC:10575) —DISRUPTS→ Sulfate Transport (GO:0015806); Sulfate Transport (GO:0015806) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002652); SLC26A3 (HGNC:10576) —DISRUPTS→ Chloride Transport (GO:0006820); Chloride Transport (GO:0006820) —LEADS_TO→ Secretory diarrhea (HP:0011352); Sulfate Transport (GO:0015806) —LEADS_TO→ Epithelial Ion Homeostasis (GO:0007275); Chloride Transport (GO:0006820) —LEADS_TO→ Epithelial Ion Homeostasis (GO:0007275). Loss-of-function mutations in SLC26A2 disrupt sulfate transport, leading to skeletal dysplasia characteristic of atelosteogenesis type II. Concurrently, loss-of-function mutations in SLC26A3 disrupt chloride transport, causing secretory diarrhea. Both sulfate and chloride transport are critical components of epithelial ion homeostasis, representing a shared functional module at the pathway level that connects these distinct genetic defects to their respective phenotypes.
